html:
SMTO-BOOT-0018 — The installer can't use the folder chosen for Conda

GUID: 2f06166a-61a2-4247-8b97-a6c553d0b9a7
Slug: boot-conda-path-invalid
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: boot

What happened

  • The folder chosen for Conda, the tool that installs the model software, isn't a full path, or it already holds other files but no working Conda. Nothing was downloaded, and that folder wasn't touched.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you set CONDA_HOME, make sure it is a full path that starts with /, for example $HOME/miniforge3, not just miniforge3 or ./conda. The installer only accepts a full path so it can't put Conda in the wrong place by accident.
  2. If Conda is already installed, set CONDA_HOME to that Conda folder, the one that contains bin/conda. The installer reuses an existing Conda only when it finds a working conda program inside that folder.
  3. Otherwise set CONDA_HOME to a folder that doesn't exist yet, for example $HOME/miniforge3-smto, and run the installer again. A fresh Conda install needs an empty spot, so it never overwrites files that are already there.

What success looks like

  • The installer prints "Using Conda" or "Installing Conda via Miniforge in" followed by the folder you chose.

If it still fails

  • Copy the full terminal output, including the SMTO-BOOT-0018 line, the folder path it shows and the Error reference line, and send it to the person who manages your model setup. Don't delete or empty the rejected folder to make room; it may hold files another program needs.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • install-vllm.sh rejected CONDA_HOME because it is not an absolute path, or because a fresh Miniforge install would target an existing path (CONDA_HOME or the default ~/miniforge3) that has no executable bin/conda.

What this means

  • CONDA_HOME is not absolute, or a new Miniforge installation would occupy an existing path without a usable selected Conda executable. The installer rejects the selected path before downloading Miniforge or creating its destination; existing contents are preserved. An occupied path does not establish who owns it or whether repairing that installation is appropriate.

Why this can happen

  • CONDA_HOME is not absolute, or a new Miniforge installation would occupy an existing path without a usable selected Conda executable.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the absolute directory and existing contents without overwriting an unrelated installation.

How to fix it

  • Set CONDA_HOME to an absolute path: either an existing Conda root with an executable bin/conda, or a path that does not exist yet for the Miniforge install (when CONDA_HOME is unset, the default target is ~/miniforge3). Do not remove or overwrite the occupied directory; the installer cannot tell who owns it, and nothing was downloaded.
  • Set CONDA_HOME to the intended absolute installation directory. Preserve existing directories that do not contain usable Conda and choose a new location.

Retry and execution caution

  • Select a usable existing Conda installation or an unused absolute destination; preserve unrelated files.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported existing Conda or a deliberate unused absolute destination is selected.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The installer rejects the selected path before downloading Miniforge or creating its destination; existing contents are preserved.
  • An occupied path does not establish who owns it or whether repairing that installation is appropriate.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
